title: PGFuzz, NDSS 2021
locator: Abstract; Sec. I (fail-safe MTL example and distance metrics); Sec. III threat model (self-sabotaging inputs out of scope); Table II policy list incl. A.RC.FS1/FS2, A.GPS.FS1, PX.GPS.FS1/FS2, A.ALIVE; Sec. VI implementation (Pymavlink, three autopilots); Table VII bug summary
evidence_grade: B for the inspected sections (peer-reviewed venue, method and policy table read directly)
finding: PGFuzz fuzzes commands, parameters and environment against 56 MTL policies per autopilot, with a distance metric to a policy violation. Its failsafe policies are per-autopilot and per-trigger (RC throttle below FS_THR_VALUE, GPS satellite count, COM_POS_FS_DELAY); no policy in Table II expresses an equivalent recovery intention ACROSS autopilots or configurations, and no GCS/offboard link-loss policy appears. The distance metric measures proximity to a single policy violation, not calibrated coverage of a recovery trajectory. Behaviour after a lost input returns is not a policy.

title: Fail-operational drone swarm architecture, 2026 v1
locator: Sec. III-C Formal Derivation of Safety Contracts, eq. (6) Communication Contract (heartbeat timestamp + SNR -> Return-To-Base); Sec. V-D ConOps verification
evidence_grade: C (architectural framework; the link-loss contract is derived, not empirically exercised against an autopilot)
finding: Defines a Communication Contract: if the last valid swarm-mesh heartbeat is older than a bound or SNR is below threshold, the FMU enforces Return-To-Base. This is an explicit link-loss -> recovery intention written as a contract, which is the closest conceptual neighbour to a composed failsafe contract found in the set. It is swarm-mesh heartbeat, not GCS/offboard link; it is one architecture, not a comparison across pinned autopilot configurations; and the paper's verification scenario (V-D) is actuator degradation, not link loss.

title: PGFuzz code repository
version: github.com/purseclab/PGFuzz at commit 7eaebf21116087249b8329d4ba7337a24a34ecb9 (2023-09-18), shallow clone 2026-09-15, 1327 files; not executed
locator: README.md (Cases 1-2: parachute; PX4 GPS fail-safe COM_POS_FS_DELAY; Sec. 6 bitcode notes); ArduPilot/fuzzing.py L145-200 (Current_policy selector, check_liveness: no HEARTBEAT for 5 s => 'program crashed' => reboot) and policy blocks A.CHUTE, A.RTL1-4, A.FLIP1-4, A.ALT_HOLD1-2, A.CIRCLE1-3/7, A.LAND1-2, A.AUTO1, A.GPS.FS1-2 (L1850-1930), A.RC.FS1-2 (L1931-1990: FS_THR_VALUE vs RC channel 3, RC_failsafe flag), A.SPORT1, A.GUIDED1, A.LOITER1, A.DRIFT1, A.BRAKE1; PX4/fuzzing.py L126-165 and blocks PX.CHUTE, PX.RTL1, PX.ALTITUDE1, PX.HOLD1-2, PX.POSITION1, PX.TAKEOFF1-2, PX.LAND1, PX.GPS.FS1-3 (L1738-1830: GPS_loss, gps_failsafe flag, COM_POS_FS_DELAY, RC channels, ALTCTL mode); PX4/check_policy.py (FLIP altitude and RTL-altitude policies); ArduPilot/update_distance.py (per-policy altitude/roll/pitch/heading error distance)
evidence_grade: C (released research code, read not run; policy set in code is narrower than the paper's Table II)
finding: Released code holds separate ArduPilot/ and PX4/ trees with separate hard-coded policy lists and MAVLink handlers; no shared policy vocabulary or mapping between the two. RC and GPS fail-safe policies from U2 Table II are implemented (A.RC.FS1-2, A.GPS.FS1-2, PX.GPS.FS1-3) as state predicates over telemetry and parameters (FS_THR_VALUE vs RC throttle, GPS status, COM_POS_FS_DELAY, mode) that score distance to a policy violation; the fuzzer drives them by mutating parameters, commands and simulated environment, not by cutting a GCS/offboard link or a setpoint stream. No A.ALIVE identifier exists in the released Python; heartbeat absence (5 s) is a crash oracle that reboots the simulator. Distance guidance is per-policy state error, matching U2's policy-violation distance. Nothing about reconnection or command return; no cross-autopilot policy equivalence.

title: ADGFuzz: Assignment Dependency-Guided Fuzzing for Robotic Vehicles, NDSS 2026
locator: Abstract; Sec. I; Sec. III-C threat model (GCS spoofing / link hijacking named as attacker tactics, out of the bug class studied); Sec. IV (MIS entropy scheduling; oracles: crash on ground, route deviation over a 7 s window, software crash = no heartbeat for 2 s); Sec. VI-A setup (ArduPilot Copter/Plane/Rover SITL, MAVProxy GCS, MAVLink); Sec. VI-B/false positives (SYSID_THISMAV breaking GCS communication excluded as false positive); Sec. VIII-C portability (PX4 named as a target, not evaluated); Appendix Table bug 40 (Rover FENCE_RADIUS/FENCE_ENABLE: fence violation detected but RTL not triggered)
evidence_grade: B for the inspected sections (peer-reviewed venue, method, setup and bug table read directly)
finding: Fuzzes ArduPilot-only (Copter, Plane, Rover in SITL) for assignment-statement bugs using a static assignment dependency graph and entropy-scheduled matched input sets. Heartbeat absence is used as a crash ORACLE (2 s), never injected as a fault; loss of GCS communication caused by SYSID_THISMAV is classified as a false positive and excluded. One reported bug (Rover, bug 40) is a failsafe-behaviour defect (fence violation without RTL), found as a bug instance, not as a comparison of recovery behaviour across configurations. No PX4 evaluation, no reconnection or command-return phase, no coverage measure of a recovery trajectory (coverage in the paper means code/MIS coverage).

title: PGPatch: Policy-Guided Logic Bug Patching for Robotic Vehicles, IEEE S&P 2022
version: Author-posted PDF S&P22_hskim.pdf from kimhyungsub.github.io (publisher copy closed: OpenAlex oa_status=closed, Semantic Scholar openAccessPdf empty, IEEE landing bot-blocked HTTP 202); 20 pages; author list matches Crossref
locator: Abstract; Sec. I (PX4 GPS fail-safe / COM_POS_FS_DELAY example); Sec. II/III (PPL formulas: PX4 GPS fail-safe, ArduPilot battery fail-safe -> RTL, sailboat pre-arm, tilt in LAND/RTL); Sec. IV term-to-code mapping table incl. Copter::failsafe_gcs_check() and failsafe_battery_event(); Sec. VI-F (Paparazzi PP.FailSafe formula 'If GPSloss and RCvalid false then mode is FAILSAFE'; extra formula for correct operation under fail-safe mode); Appendix Table VIII Paparazzi FAILSAFE bugs
evidence_grade: B for the inspected sections (peer-reviewed venue, author-posted full text read directly)
finding: Automated program repair for logic bugs in ArduPilot, PX4 and Paparazzi, driven by per-autopilot PPL formulas. Fail-safe requirements appear as autopilot-specific formulas in each autopilot's own parameter and mode vocabulary (COM_POS_FS_DELAY / GPSfail; FS_BATT_ENABLE / RTL; PP.FailSafe), and patch verification checks 'correct operation under fail-safe mode'. This is the nearest neighbour in FORM to a per-autopilot recovery contract, but no formula is defined as equivalent across autopilots or pinned configurations, no comparison of realised behaviour is made, and the ArduPilot GCS-failsafe function appears only as a code-mapping location. Link loss and setpoint loss are not injected; what happens when inputs return is not a formula; no trajectory coverage measure.
